verdict.reasoning: Headache onset this morning about four hours ago and left-sided: “This morning… about four hours ago, you've developed a headache… on the left side of the head?” / Patient: “Yep… Yeah.” Sudden onset: “did it come on suddenly?” Patient: “Yeah, yeah, yeah.”

Sudden onset: “did it come on suddenly?… Patient: “Yeah, yeah, yeah.” Pain 6/10: “maybe five, well, six, six probably.” Not clearly retro-orbital: when asked “is it behind the eye?” patient answers “Uh, no, no it's… I don't know how to describe it.”

Blurred vision with zigzag lines: “My vision is quite blurred… some zigzag lines.” Dizziness: “I feel like um, uh, dizzy.” Nausea/vomiting twice at onset: “I vomit twice… as soon as the, the headache started, I also vomited… and I still feel nausea.” Worsened with movement and prefers head still: “if I leave bed, I start to feel like, even worse if I move… I just want to have my… head like really, uh, not moving.” Cannot tolerate screens: “I cannot stand screens.”

No prior similar headaches: “Have you ever had a headache like this in the past?… Patient: ‘well not, really… like this, no, definitely. It's something new.’” Denies limb weakness or gait disturbance: “have you noticed any weakness in your arms or legs…? Patient: ‘No, no , no, no.’… ‘when you're walking…?’ Patient: ‘Uh, not really.’ Doctor summarizes: “you've got no neurological symptoms. You're walking fine.”

History of kidney stones: Patient uses it as pain reference and doctor reiterates: “Well, I had the kidney stone, so let's say that that's ten.” Doctor: “You've mentioned, in the past, you've had kidney stones…”
Mother with migraines: “my mother has migraines. I'm not sure if that's relevant?” and later repeated: “you mentioned your mother has migraines.”
Family history of hypothyroidism: “also, I have hypothyroidism in the family… She also has Hypothyroidism.”
No regular medications: “And do you take any regular medications? Patient: ‘Uh, no.’”

Paracetamol about 3 hours ago without relief: “what time did you take the paracetamol?… headache started like… four hours ago. So, I would say like, maybe three hours ago… because I couldn't stand it.” Lack of relief: “I tried Paracetemol, but uh, didn't work. To be honest, I feel exactly the same.”
No known drug allergies: “Are you allergic to any medications? Patient: ‘Not that I'm aware… Yeah, not that I'm aware.’”

Doctor’s assessment of probable migraine with visual aura: “it sounds like what you're suffering from is what's known as a migraine… the reason why this sounds like migraines is because it's on one side of the head… you've got blurry vision… with the nausea and vomiting.” First episode, no focal neurology: patient denies previous similar headaches and doctor states “you've got no neurological symptoms. You're walking fine.” Visual disturbance and movement sensitivity are documented elsewhere in the transcript.

Ibuprofen and antiemetic from pharmacy: “I would recommend… if you take some medications, maybe something like ibuprofen?… there's lots of medication treatments so, there's, it can be ibuprofen with an anti-sickness… which you can get from the pharmacy.”
Sugary carbonated drink: “and you also to drink, uh, sugary and carbonated drinks, something like Coke.”

Same-day in-person review: “we would want to see you, um, as soon as possible, to do like a full neurological exam… assessment to where we can see you today at some point.” This implies arranging a same-day in-person review for full neurological exam.

Cancel if improved: “however, if you do take these medications and… by the time your appointment time comes in and you feel much better in yourself, you can cancel it, um, you can give us a call and cancel it.”
Contact clinic if ongoing problems: “any further problems between now and your appointment, please do let us know.” This covers persisting or worsening symptoms before the appointment.

Consider escalation to specific migraine therapies: “For the three of them is… a good sort of cocktail to start them, then we can go up the treatment ladder, you can get specific migraine relief medication. And that should be something to try between now and when we see you to do the… assessment.”
Pregnancy unlikely: “Is there any chance you could be pregnant? Patient: ‘Uh, I really doubt it.’”
